_placeholderNote: As of 2026-08-09, categoryScores/overallScore are computed by a fixed, documented formula from boolean evidence facts (not manual per-company judgment), so every point is traceable to a specific finding. The formula was rebalanced on 2026-08-09 for a wider, more honest spread: neutral baselines (no evidence either way) sit around 43-46; confirmed negative evidence (e.g. a regulatory privacy fine) pulls a company down into the high-30s; multiple confirmed positive facts push a company up into the 60s-70s. Category maxes are unchanged (Labor Displacement 30, Data Privacy 25, Human Oversight 25, Transparency 20) - only the internal baselines/coefficients per fact changed: laborDisplacement = 13 + 9 (reskillingFunded) - 16 (aiLayoffTracked); dataPrivacy = 18 + 6 (noAiTrainingOnPersonalData) + 4 (dedicatedAiTrainingOptOut) - 9 (tosScrapingOptOut) - 18 (confirmedPrivacyFine); humanOversight = 9 + 9 (humanInTheLoopMandate) + 6 (dedicatedAiGovernanceBody) + 5 (noConsequentialAutomatedDecisions); transparency = 6 + min(policyCitationCount,4) + 7 (recurringPublicAiReport) + 6 (concreteTransparencyArtifacts) - 3 (fewer than 3 total citations), each clamped to its category max. No company currently has strong evidence across 3+ of the 4 categories at once, so 80+ isn't reachable honestly yet - that would require crediting categories with no supporting evidence, which we won't do. 11 of 20 companies (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Meta, JPMorgan Chase, Walmart, Visa, Broadcom, Johnson & Johnson, Home Depot) have real evidence for at least one of the newer facts; the other 9 (Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, Tesla, Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth, Mastercard, Exxon Mobil, Costco, Procter & Gamble) were genuinely researched but yielded no qualifying new facts (blocked pages, or generic policy language that didn't meet the bar), so they default to false and tie with each other - that reflects identical evidence, not a scoring bug.

citations.snippet: Dell Technologies maintains a comprehensive global privacy program. The Privacy Statement covers collection, use, sharing, and protection of personal information. The Privacy Center provides tools for consumers to manage their data preferences including CCPA opt-out ('My Privacy Choices'). Dell's AI tools operate under the firm's data governance and privacy framework.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - ~220,000 Employees; Human Capital and Efficiency Initiatives
citations.snippet: Wells Fargo employs approximately 220,000 full-time equivalent employees as of December 31, 2025. The company has been executing multi-year efficiency initiatives under CEO Charles Scharf, reducing headcount by approximately 30,000 from peak levels through attrition and targeted reductions. These reductions are attributed to business streamlining and cost management, not AI automation. Not in the layoffs.fyi AI tracker.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - AI Strategy: Risk Management, Customer Service, Back-Office
citations.snippet: Wells Fargo uses artificial intelligence and machine learning across risk management, fraud detection, customer service, and operational efficiency. The company's AI use is subject to its model risk management framework and regulatory guidance. AI risks include potential bias, model failure, and regulatory scrutiny. Wells Fargo discloses AI-related risks in its risk factor disclosures and discusses AI governance within its enterprise risk management program.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - Cybersecurity; Technology Risk and Board Oversight
citations.snippet: Wells Fargo's Risk Committee of the Board of Directors oversees technology risk including cybersecurity. The company's Chief Technology Officer and Chief Information Security Officer lead cybersecurity programs with board-level reporting. Wells Fargo maintains a comprehensive information security program aligned with industry frameworks. Cybersecurity risk is integrated into the enterprise risk management system with regular Audit and Risk Committee reporting.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - Regulatory Consent Orders: Efficiency/Compliance, Not AI-Privacy
citations.snippet: Wells Fargo remains subject to the Federal Reserve asset cap consent order (2018) related to governance failures and prior sales practice violations. The 2022 $3.7B CFPB consent order addressed improper fees, mortgage servicing failures, and auto loan irregularities. Neither constitutes a confirmed AI or customer data-privacy fine under Regulation S-P, GDPR, or CCPA. Wells Fargo has not been subject to a significant privacy enforcement action specifically related to AI or data-protection violations.

citations.title: Wells Fargo Privacy Policy
citations.snippet: Wells Fargo's privacy policy covers collection, use, and sharing of personal information for customers and website visitors. The policy complies with GLBA, CCPA, and applicable financial services data privacy requirements. Wells Fargo offers California residents the right to limit sharing of personal information. The policy describes data practices for financial products and services.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - ~35,000 Employees; Clean Energy Portfolio
citations.snippet: GE Vernova, spun off from General Electric on April 2, 2024, employs approximately 35,000 people globally. The company operates three segments: Wind, Electrification, and Gas Power. GE Vernova is focused on clean energy transition providing wind turbines, grid solutions, and gas power technologies. Not in the layoffs.fyi AI tracker. Any workforce adjustments in 2024-2025 were related to business restructuring post-separation, not AI-attributed layoffs.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - AI Use in Energy Systems; Grid Optimization and Digital Products
citations.snippet: GE Vernova deploys AI and machine learning in grid management, wind farm optimization, and predictive maintenance for power generation equipment. The company's digital products unit provides software solutions that leverage AI for energy system management. AI use is primarily for improving operational efficiency of power and grid equipment rather than automating internal workforce roles.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - Cybersecurity and Technology Risk Management
citations.snippet: GE Vernova maintains a cybersecurity program aligned with NIST Cybersecurity Framework. The company's Board of Directors and Audit Committee oversee cybersecurity risk management. As a newly independent company following the April 2024 spin-off from GE, GE Vernova has been establishing standalone cybersecurity, data governance, and compliance programs independent of former GE systems.

citations.title: Form 10-K FY2025 - ESG and Sustainability Reporting; Clean Energy Mission
citations.snippet: GE Vernova publishes sustainability disclosures aligned with its mission to electrify and decarbonize the world. The company reports on emissions, workforce safety, and governance. As a recently spun-off entity, GE Vernova is developing its standalone ESG reporting framework. No confirmed AI-specific transparency artifacts or recurring public AI accountability reports as of fiscal year 2025.

citations.title: GE Vernova Privacy Statement
citations.snippet: GE Vernova's privacy statement governs the collection, use, and protection of personal data for customers, employees, and website visitors. The company complies with GDPR, CCPA, and applicable data protection laws globally. Privacy rights include access, correction, and deletion requests as applicable. The company's data governance practices were established following the 2024 separation from General Electric.
